We focus on how you can choose your career to have the *greatest* impact whether by focusing on alleviating global poverty, trying to prevent future pandemics, trying to prevent nuclear war, and lots more. Every semester we run a seminar that outlines all of the areas in which you can have the most impact with your career. 		28 text Licensing Exams
	29 text In order to become an amateur radio operator in the United States, you must first pass one or more multiple-choice exams to obtain a license from the FCC. These exams cover basic theory of electronics and radio, as well as FCC rules, and are administered by groups of volunteer examiners around the country, including a group here at Carnegie Mellon. We offer exams for Technician, General, and Extra class licenses. You can take any or all of the exams for a single fee. Knowledge of Morse code is no longer required to obtain an amateur radio license in the U.S.

					159 text Chhavi Yadav : Benchmarking Agent Susceptibility to Decomposition Attacks
					160 text Abstract
					161 text LLM-based agents are becoming increasingly capable and widely deployed, creating growing incentives for adversarial misuse in the real world. A key emerging threat is decomposition attacks, in which a harmful task is broken into simpler, benign subtasks that evade safety mechanisms when executed separately but cumulatively fulfill the malicious intent. Although recent benchmarks assess agent safety in multi-turn and multi-tool-use settings, they do not explicitly capture this form of decompositional misuse and may not represent realistic adversarial execution flows. To this end, we introduce DeCompBench, a benchmark designed specifically to evaluate agentic safety under decomposition attacks. DeCompBench is created with a decomposition-by-design principle using a graphical framework, and it enables harmful task decomposition into individually benign and executable subtasks with realistic workflows. Our experiments using a prompt-based LLM decomposer show that state-of-the-art agents exhibit high refusal rates on monolithic harmful tasks but significantly lower refusal rates on their decomposed variants, often inadvertently fulfilling the adversarial objectives. These findings underscore the need for safety evaluations against decomposition attacks and corresponding defenses. Our dataset is available at 
					162 link Description: https://huggingface.co/datasets/decompositionbench/DeCompBench, Value: huggingface.co/datasets/decompositionbench/DeCompBench
					163 text .
					164 text Bio
					165 text Chhavi Yadav is a Postdoctoral Researcher in the Machine Learning Department (MLD) at Carnegie Mellon University, where she focuses on AI safety, security, and privacy. She earned her PhD in Computer Science from UC San Diego in 2025, where she received the UCSD CSE Doctoral Excellence in Research Award. Her work has been recognized with an NCWIT Collegiate Award (Finalist, 2025), an AAAI Doctoral Consortium Award (2025), a Rising Star in Data Science Award (2024), a Best Paper Award at the ICLR 2024 Privacy Workshop, and a Best Paper Honorable Mention at the NeurIPS 2019 ML4Health Workshop. 			28 text The Bangladeshi Student Organization (BSO) at Carnegie Mellon University aims to provide a home for students and faculty of Bengali descent. 				50 text Members Benefits
			51 text Becoming a member of the Bangladeshi Student Organization (BSO) at CMU offers students a chance to connect with a supportive and vibrant community. Members can celebrate traditional Bangladeshi festivals such as Eid, Pohela Boishakh, and International Mother Language Day, fostering a strong cultural connection even while away from home. BSO also creates a welcoming space for all CMU students—regardless of background—who are interested in exploring Bangladeshi culture through food, music, storytelling, and shared experiences. Members benefit from opportunities to grow as leaders by organizing events and taking part in community outreach. In addition, the organization provides a valuable network for professional connections and personal friendships, helping students find both support and joy during their time at CMU.
